chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from 'Ubaydullah al-Halabi from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him): In the case of
a man who is behind the Imam, and the Imam prolongs the Tashahhud, he (peace be upon him) said: 'Those behind him should offer the salam, and if they wish, they may proceed with their need.'

key_terms.التَّشَهُّد: Tashahhud (the sitting portion of prayer where testimonies are recited)
key_terms.خَلْفَ الْإِمَام: Behind the Imam (standing in congregation behind the leader of prayer)
key_terms.يُسَلِّم: To offer the salam (concluding the prayer by turning the head)

ai.seo_question: What should a worshipper do if the Imam prolongs the Tashahhud during prayer?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on *Ahkam al-Sahw* (rulings for forgetfulness/distraction), this hadith clarifies the flexibility for followers (muqtadis) when the Imam prolongs the Tashahhud. It establishes that while the follower may conclude their prayer independently by offering the salam, they are not compelled to remain if they have a pressing need, reflecting the Shia principle of ease in worship.
